<p class="lede">Cook Inlet in Alaska had about 1,300 belugas in 1979. Recent surveys count about 300 to 400.</p>
<p class="scroll-hint" aria-hidden="true">&#8595;</p>

<section class="data-section" aria-label="Cook Inlet belugas, Arctic sea ice, shipping and ocean temperature by year">
<p id="year" class="year"></p>

```{=html}
<div class="stats" id="stats"></div>
<svg id="plot" class="plot" viewBox="0 0 600 250" role="img" aria-label="Cook Inlet belugas, Arctic sea ice, shipping and ocean temperature by year. One bold line for the whales and thinner lines for pressures."></svg>
<div class="slider-row">
<button id="sweep" class="sweep" type="button" aria-label="Play timeline">&#9654;</button>
<input id="slider" class="slider" type="range" step="1" aria-label="Year">
</div>
```

<p class="note">The bold line is the Cook Inlet belugas, the longest yearly survey series for the species; no yearly count exists worldwide. Estimates before 2004 used earlier methods. Each line is drawn against its own range, so compare shapes, not heights.</p>
<noscript><p>The full table is in the data folder.</p></noscript>
</section>

<footer>
<p><strong>Data.</strong> Cook Inlet belugas: 1979 estimate from Calkins (1989), cited in the <a href="https://media.fisheries.noaa.gov/2022-09/cibw-5-year-review-2022.pdf">NOAA 5-year review (2022)</a>; 1994 to 2003 from <a href="https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/resource/data/aerial-surveys-belugas-cook-inlet">NOAA aerial surveys</a> (Hobbs et al.); 2004 to 2022 from <a href="https://media.fisheries.noaa.gov/2023-06/PR2023-03.pdf">Goetz et al. (2023)</a>, whose recommended best estimate is 331. Sea ice: <a href="https://nsidc.org/data/g02135">NSIDC Sea Ice Index</a>, September extent. Shipping: total goods loaded, <a href="https://unctad.org/system/files/official-document/rmt2021_en_0.pdf">UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport</a> (2021, 2024 and 2025 editions); years without a published total are bridged with a straight line. Ocean temperature: <a href="https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/climate-at-a-glance/global/time-series">NOAA Climate at a Glance</a>, global ocean, yearly, against the 1901 to 2000 average. <a href="data/beluga-series.csv">Download the table</a>. The call is synthesized from a published spectrogram, not a recording.</p>
</footer>
